qs.q:
My university days — During their university days, which person…

A=Annabelle (no scholarship, dormitory, didn't get on with others, started volunteering in library, found passion for reading)
B=Bradley (garage band rehearsals, parents stopped funding, pulled self together, scholarship, no problem finding job)
C=Cheryl (financially independent via grandma's trust fund, busgirl at tavern with guitarist, boyfriend left, found comfort in studies)
D=Dominic (enrolled dream uni, uncle leased apartment, met life partner, struggled with workload, friends moved on)
E=Elaine (took student loan, sports/bars, then realised had to graduate, met lifelong friends in library)
F=Forrest (parents supported, devoted to studies, learned importance of healthy body from dormitory friends, joined squash club)

0. helped out in the library? [A=Annabelle]
1. had a job?
2. went out a lot?
3. took up sports?
4. had a grant?
5. lived in a dormitory?
6. made friends for life?
7. was disappointed in love?
8. admired their professors?
9. was a member of a band?
10. left college without graduating?
11. lost the support of their family?
12. longed for their high-school friends?
items: 9 — was a member of a band?
11 — lost the support of their family?

qs.q:
Our home-schooling story

"I wanted to hear about their dreams, but instead had to wake them before they could remember them... I wanted to give them my complete attention, but instead had to tell them to HURRY UP AND LEAVE."

What did the writer see as the biggest problem when her children started going to school?
A Having to give up her career.
B Doing homework at late hours.
C Missing her two children.
D Getting up early in the morning.
opts: Having to give up her career.
Doing homework at late hours.
Missing her two children.
Getting up early in the morning.

qs.q:
Our home-schooling story

"Due to CONSIDERABLE LOSS OF INCOME, we ended up sending him back to 2nd grade in the previous school."

What influenced the parents' decision about their younger son's second school year?
A A new school had opened nearby.
B They had financial difficulties.
C Their son got a new teacher.
D Their son regained his self-esteem.
opts: A new school had opened nearby.
They had financial difficulties.
Their son got a new teacher.
Their son regained his self-esteem.

qs.q:
Our home-schooling story

"She thought the SCORE OF 25% WAS ACCEPTABLE. We decided to never again leave our children's success or failure to the school system."

What made the parents finally choose home schooling?
A Their son had a low result in a maths test.
B The school's expectations were too low.
C They disliked the school's testing system.
D They wanted better grades for their son.
opts: Their son had a low result in a maths test.
The school's expectations were too low.
They disliked the school's testing system.
They wanted better grades for their son.

qs.q:
Our home-schooling story

"Home schooling gave us the flexibility to relocate... when my HUSBAND DECIDED TO LEAVE HIS JOB to start his own business."

Why did the family move home after starting to home-school their children?
A Because the mother had lost her job.
B Because they did not have enough money.
C Because of their sons' health.
D Because of the father's career.
opts: Because the mother had lost her job.
Because they did not have enough money.
Because of their sons' health.
Because of the father's career.

qs.q:
Our home-schooling story

"I discovered a new trait in me – I have a bit of an independent streak when it comes to SCHEDULING OUR LIFE. I love being able to DECIDE WHEN TO DO WHAT."

What does the writer see as the biggest advantage of home schooling according to paragraph 5?
A She is in charge of organising the time.
B The children learn to follow the rules.
C The children have better chances of getting into a good college.
D Home schooling is cheaper than other ways of schooling.
opts: She is in charge of organising the time.
The children learn to follow the rules.
The children have better chances of getting into a good college.
Home schooling is cheaper than other ways of schooling.

qs.q:
Our home-schooling story

"They YEARN for spelling bees, science fairs and talent shows. Although I know they are excelling, THEY CAN'T TELL HOW GOOD THEY ARE."

What do we find out about the writer's children from the final paragraph?
A They do not have much social interaction.
B They like to spend time on their grandparents' farm.
C They are not good at applying what they've learned.
D They would like to compare themselves with their peers.
opts: They do not have much social interaction.
They like to spend time on their grandparents' farm.
They are not good at applying what they've learned.
They would like to compare themselves with their peers.

qs.q:
Why do some people learn faster?

"The first reaction appears immediately after a mistake and is the inevitable response to any lapse. (19) ____. It occurs when we pay attention to the error, dwelling on the disappointing result."

A Simply commending someone for 'being' smart stimulates the wish to 'look' smart.
B This meant that the experience of failure had been so discouraging that instead of improving, they regressed.
C The second signal arrives later and is associated with awareness.
D This inevitably implies that the extra awareness always pays dividends in performance.
E However, it induces frequent mistakes, as the boring procedure encourages people to zone out.
F Education is neither magic nor is it the wisdom derived from failure.
G The other has a growth mind-set and they believe that we can get better at almost anything.
H Unless we experience the unpleasant symptoms of being wrong, our mind will never revise its models.
opts: A — Being commended for being smart stimulates the wish to look smart.
B — The experience of failure was so discouraging they regressed.
C — The second signal arrives later and is associated with awareness.
D — Extra awareness always pays dividends in performance.
E — It induces frequent mistakes as the boring procedure encourages people to zone out.
F — Education is neither magic nor wisdom derived from failure.
G — The other has a growth mind-set and believes we can get better.
H — Unless we experience the symptoms of being wrong, our mind won't revise its models.

D Extra awareness always pays dividends.
E It induces frequent mistakes.
F Education is neither magic nor wisdom.

H Unless we experience the symptoms of being wrong, our mind won't revise its models.
opts: A — Being commended for being smart stimulates the wish to look smart.

D — Extra awareness always pays dividends.
E — It induces frequent mistakes.
F — Education is neither magic nor wisdom.
G — The other has a growth mind-set and believes we can get better at almost anything, provided we invest time and energy.
H — Unless we experience the symptoms of being wrong, our mind won't revise its models.
